caption:
Kling and Seedance are the two AI video models most people try after the big US apps.
Kling 4.0 makes longer clips in one pass. Seedance 2.0 takes more kinds of references and makes the sound with the picture.
Here is which one fits what you want to make.

Which AI video tool do you use most?

threads_text: Kling 4.0 makes clips up to 30 seconds in one pass. Seedance 2.0 stops at 15 seconds but mixes images, video and audio references and generates stereo sound with the picture. Which one do you reach for first?

slides.headline: *Kling vs Seedance*: which AI video model to use, and what each one costs

slides.heading: 1. Kling goes *longer*
paras: Kling 4.0 makes clips of 3 to 30 seconds in one pass, with up to 10 keyframes.
Its Omni Reference takes up to 15 assets: images, videos, subjects and voices.

slides.heading: 2. Seedance mixes *everything*
paras: Seedance 2.0 takes text plus up to 9 images, 3 video clips and 3 audio clips in one request.
It returns up to 15 seconds of multi-shot video with stereo sound.

slides.heading: 3. What *free* gets you
paras: Kling's free Basic plan has no monthly credits. Paid plans start with 660 credits a month.
Dreamina lets you start Seedance with no credit card, and its Lite model runs on trial credits.

site_article.headline: Kling vs Seedance: which AI video model to use, with plans and limits compared
site_article.dek: Kling 4.0 makes longer clips and gives you keyframes. Seedance 2.0 takes the widest mix of references and makes the sound with the picture. Here is how to pick.
site_article.summary: Kling 4.0 generates clips of up to 30 seconds in one pass with up to 10 keyframes and 15 reference assets. Seedance 2.0 makes clips of up to 15 seconds from text, images, video and audio together, with stereo sound.
site_article.seo_title: Kling vs Seedance: which AI video model to use in 2026
site_article.seo_description: Kling vs Seedance compared: clip length, references, sound, free credits, plan prices and real face rules, plus prompts to test both models on the same shot.
site_article.answer_summary: Pick Kling if you need clips longer than 15 seconds, keyframe control or Kling's per second credit pricing. Pick Seedance 2.0 if you want to combine images, video and audio references in one request and get stereo sound generated with the picture.
site_article.hero_alt: Kling 4.0 promotional header image for its AI video generation feature.

paragraphs.text: Kling vs Seedance is the choice most people face once they move past the AI video tools built into the big US chatbots. Kling is the video model from the Chinese company Kuaishou, and its newest version, Kling 4.0, launched for all users on October 15, 2026 after an early access phase that began on September 30. Seedance is ByteDance's video model. Its Seed team launched Seedance 2.0 on February 12, 2026, and consumers reach it through Dreamina, ByteDance's image and video site.

The short answer: Kling is the better pick when you need a longer clip or precise control over where the shot goes. Seedance is the better pick when you want to throw a pile of references at the model, including a voice or a piece of music, and get the sound back with the picture.
Kling vs Seedance at a glance

Clip length: Kling says Kling 4.0 generates natively from 3 to 30 seconds in a single pass, and that video extension forward or backward will reach up to 2 minutes in total. Kling's older VIDEO 3.0 model runs from 3 to 15 seconds. Seedance 2.0 returns up to 15 seconds of multi-shot video, according to ByteDance's launch post.

References: Kling 4.0's Omni Reference accepts up to 15 assets combined. Kling's FAQ breaks that down as up to 10 images, up to 5 reference videos with a combined length of up to 30 seconds, and up to 7 subject elements, and it also takes voices. You can set up to 10 keyframes. Seedance 2.0 takes text plus up to 9 images, 3 video clips and 3 audio clips in one generation. Dreamina says each video or audio reference can be up to 15 seconds long.

Sound: Seedance 2.0 makes the audio together with the video. ByteDance describes dual channel stereo with separate tracks for music, ambience, effects and character voices. Kling's VIDEO 3.0 also has Native Audio, which covers dialogue, lip sync, ambience and sound effects, and its guide lists speech in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Spanish, with dialects and accents. Kling's Kling 4.0 page does not describe audio.
Picture: Kling 4.0 offers 21:9, 16:9, 1:1 and 9:16 frames. Its page marks native 4K, 1080p and 10 bit HDR output as coming soon. Dreamina says Seedance 2.0 videos download at 1080p.
Free credits and prices

Kling sells credits through monthly plans. Its credit guide, dated July 28, 2026, lists a free Basic plan with no monthly credits and output that is not for commercial use. The Standard plan, listed from $6.99 a month, comes with 660 credits, which Kling says is about 33 videos at 720p, and adds 1080p, watermark removal and commercial use. Pro comes with 3,000 credits, Premier with 8,000 and Ultra with 26,000. Native 4K on VIDEO 3.0 costs 30 credits a second.
Kling had not announced pricing for Kling 4.0 when it launched, according to Let's Data Science, so check the credit cost shown in the app before you generate with it.

Dreamina says you can start Seedance with no credit card. It also offers a lighter model, listed as Seedance 2.0 Lite on one page and Seedance 2.0 mini in its menus, which it describes as faster and cheaper to run and free to try with trial credits. Dreamina's menus also list a newer Seedance 2.5.

Neither one is truly free for regular use. On Kling, the free plan gives you an account but no monthly credits. On Dreamina, trial credits are enough to test a few ideas. If you only need a handful of clips, start on Seedance Lite; if you plan to generate every week, compare Kling's monthly credits with the cost per clip that Dreamina shows you before you pay.
Which one to pick

paragraphs.title: 1. You need a clip longer than 15 seconds
paragraphs.text: Use Kling 4.0. It is the only one of the two that generates up to 30 seconds in one pass, so you avoid stitching two clips that do not quite match.

paragraphs.title: 2. You want to control exactly where the shot goes
paragraphs.text: Use Kling 4.0 and set keyframes. Up to 10 of them let you pin the frames the video has to pass through.

paragraphs.title: 3. You have a voice, a song or a sound to match
paragraphs.text: Use Seedance 2.0. Upload the audio clip next to your images and refer to each file in the prompt by name with an @ sign, the way Dreamina's guide shows (@AssetName).

paragraphs.title: 4. You just want to try AI video today
paragraphs.text: Open Dreamina and pick the Lite or mini model. It runs on trial credits, and the steps are the same as for the full model.
Prompts to test both on the same shot

The fairest test is one prompt in both tools at the same length. Keep it to one subject, one camera move and one sound, so you can see which model handles the basics better before you spend credits on a long scene.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: One subject, one camera move
paragraphs.text: A slow push-in on [subject] in [place] at [time of day], soft light from the left. At the third second, [subject] turns and looks at the camera. Quiet ambient sound of [place].

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: A product from one photo
paragraphs.text: [Product] sits on a wooden kitchen counter in morning light. The camera circles slowly to the left. Steam rises from a cup beside it. Soft acoustic guitar music.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: A short line of dialogue
paragraphs.text: Medium shot of [person] standing on a rainy street at night. They look up, then say in a calm voice: "[one short line]". Sound of rain and distant traffic.
Where each one falls short

ByteDance is unusually frank about Seedance 2.0. Its launch post says the model is still far from perfect: detail stability, realism and natural motion need work, keeping several subjects consistent is hard, text inside the video is not always accurate, and the audio can occasionally distort.

Using a real person's face as a Seedance reference requires identity verification or prior legal authorization, according to ByteDance. If an upload is rejected, check whether it shows a real face before you rewrite the prompt.

Kling's weak spot is cost and paperwork. Every re-roll spends credits, commercial use and watermark removal sit behind a paid plan, and some of Kling 4.0's headline features, such as two minute extension and 4K HDR, were still listed as coming when this guide was written. The quality claims for both models come from the companies themselves, so a ten minute test with your own prompt is worth more than any spec sheet.
